title: What If a Venus Probe Never Left Earth? One Fell Back 53 Years Later

scenes.text: What if a spacecraft built to land on Venus got stuck circling Earth instead? One did.
March 1972. The Soviet probe Kosmos 482 launched four days after its twin. The twin reached Venus. This one never escaped Earth orbit.
Its lander stayed in orbit: a titanium ball about a meter wide, weighing half a ton.
It was built to survive the plunge into Venus's atmosphere. So experts warned it could reach the ground in one piece.
For 53 years it circled lower. On May 10th, 2025, it came down over the Indian Ocean, Russia's space agency said.
Nobody saw it fall. Nothing was recovered. If it survived, a Venus lander now sits on the seabed.

description:
What if a spacecraft built for Venus never left Earth orbit? Kosmos 482, launched by the Soviet Union on 31 March 1972 as the twin of Venera 8, was stranded by a suspected engine failure.
Its descent capsule, a titanium-cased sphere about one meter wide and 495 kilograms, was designed to survive entry into the atmosphere of Venus, so trackers expected it might get through Earth's atmosphere intact. Roscosmos said it re-entered at 06:24 UTC on 10 May 2025 and fell into the Indian Ocean west of Jakarta. There were no eyewitness reports and no debris was recovered; analysts disagree on whether it burned up or hit the water whole at around 240 km/h or more.
